chapter: Wax Records, Broadway shows and Eddie Condon
title: Between Condon and Barefoot Boy, and the fate of the Wax masters
summary: Hall explains the timing of his jobs and what became of Wax Records, now issued in Europe.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: I'm still, you know, we are talking about this whole period in general because you were doing so many things. All right, you came off the tour with him and that's when you went into 'Barefoot Boy.'
Not exactly. I came off the tour on November 1st, when my youngest daughter was born and 'Barefoot Boy' started in March.
Of '47. So, what did you, did you just played around --
Yeah.
Around town?
Yeah, gigs.
And meanwhile, Wax Records was --
Yeah.
To get back to Wax just for a minute. So, you said Atlantic took it over many years later but is it available now in any shape or form now? Who owns it, or --
I don't know. It has been put out in album form.
Where?
In Sweden.
In Europe, yeah. No one has put it out here?
No. I had offers to do so though.
You still own the rights to it?
I don't know.
You don't know. I wonder who does?
Well, Nickey Peters I guess.
Well, where is she?

In New London, Connecticut. But the Barkley's had an interchange of sides in some of those years. I never could trace that down but then I found out it is in Europe, 20 years and your copyright's right is expired -- so, that's what they did.
Even though the product was made here they have a jurisdiction like that? That they should be able to arbitrarily take someone's work after 20 years?
Becomes public domain. It is on a label called Crystal, have you seen it?
No. We'll look at it later.
All right.
